program_name: Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering and Information Technology (EEIT). Listed on the university orientation portal as "Electrical Engineering And Information Technology (in fase di accreditamento)" — i.e. the title itself still carries the "undergoing accreditation" tag. The dedicated programme site uses the English title "Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering and Information Technology"; no separate Italian diploma title is published, because this is a newly created English-medium course (type: standalone, not an English curriculum inside an Italian degree).
teaching_language: English only — 100% of the programme is delivered in English. Federico II lists it in the "International Course Catalogue" with language tag "ENG", and the orientation portal sidebar shows "Language ENG". Italian language proficiency is NOT required: per the university's international admission regulation, for a three-year degree taught in English "level B2 Italian language proficiency is not required". Applicants must instead prove English at CEFR B2 or higher. The programme is explicitly open to Italian, EU and non-EU students. The final semester (electives + major) is also taught in English.
campus: Naples — Via Claudio 21, 80125 Napoli, at the Department of Electrical Engineering and Information Technology (DIETI). This is the Fuorigrotta engineering complex (not Monte Sant'Angelo). Administrative/enrolment counter is separate: Segreteria Studenti Area Didattica Ingegneria, Piazzale Tecchio 80, 80125 Napoli (also Fuorigrotta) — in-person enrolment happens there, weekdays 09:00–12:00. The programme sits under the School of Polytechnic and Basic Sciences (Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base, SPSB).
degree_class: L-8 (Ingegneria dell'Informazione / Information Engineering). Confirmed on the orientation portal fact-box: "Degree class L-8". Three-year first-cycle laurea (six semesters); standard Italian L-class volume of 180 CFU.
admission_type: Open access (accesso libero / no published numerus clausus) BUT with a compulsory entry test and possible OFA. There is conflicting labelling across official Federico II pages: (a) the orientation portal fact-box states "Admission TOLC - I - OFA"; (b) the university news release describes the test as "obbligatorio ma non selettivo" (compulsory but non-selective) and the programme's own "How to enroll" page repeats "Admission to the Degree Programme requires sitting an Orientation and Self-Assessment Test, which is compulsory but non-selective"; (c) the programme's "Pre-Requisites" and "Educational requirements" pages instead call the CEnT-S "the compulsory selective test, required for admission" with a hard minimum threshold of 9/45. In practice a minimum score IS applied for enrolment, so it behaves as a threshold-based (not ranking-based) admission. No seat cap has been published; the programme states only that "The Programme Teaching Committee normally defines the admission criteria and any enrolment limits". Non-EU applicants needing a visa additionally go through a selective pre-admission stage assessed by the Degree Programme Coordinator via the Universitaly portal. [uncertain]
academic_requirements: 1) Upper secondary school diploma, or an equivalent qualification obtained abroad recognised as suitable. 2) The diploma must have been awarded after AT LEAST 12 YEARS of pre-university education — this is stated repeatedly and is the single most common disqualifier for non-EU applicants. 3) For non-Italian diplomas, a "Dichiarazione di Valore" (Declaration of Value) issued by the competent Italian embassy/consulate, or as an alternative a CIMEA (Italian ENIC-NARIC centre) Certificate of Comparability. 4) Required subject preparation, formally assessed by the entry test: (a) logical ability — correctly interpreting the meaning of a text, identifying the input data of a problem and using them to reach a solution, deducing the behaviour of a simple system, linking results to the hypotheses that determine them; (b) basic scientific knowledge — properties and operations on numbers, absolute value, powers and roots, logarithms and exponentials, literal calculus, polynomials, first- and second-degree algebraic equations and inequalities, systems of first-degree equations, measure and properties of segments and angles, lines and planes, properties of the main plane and solid geometric figures, Cartesian coordinates, concept of function, equations of lines and simple geometric loci, graphs and properties of elementary and trigonometric functions, elementary physics and basic knowledge of the structure of matter. 5) EU applicants (and non-EU applicants legally resident in Italy/EU) have unrestricted access if they hold a qualification corresponding to the required Italian qualification, but must send their academic documents to the Degree Programme Coordinator for the qualification assessment (translations, legalisations, Diploma Supplement, exam certificates, CIMEA certificate, Declaration of Value as applicable). Note: prior study of engineering is not required; the first five semesters are foundational.
language_requirements: English at CEFR B2 or higher is MANDATORY for both EU and non-EU candidates: "Candidate students should provide evidence of English language proficiency at B2 or higher (CEFR level)." Italian is NOT required (B2 Italian is waived for English-taught degrees). Accepted certificate issuers recognised by Federico II: Cambridge Assessment English; City and Guilds (Pitman); Edexcel/Pearson Ltd; Educational Testing Service (ETS); English Speaking Board (ESB); IELTS; Pearson; Trinity College London; Department of English, Faculty of Arts – University of Malta; NQAI–ACELS (Ireland); Ascentis; AIM Awards; Learning Resource Network (LRN); British Institutes; British Council EnglishScore; Gatehouse Awards Ltd; TOEFL; LanguageCert; ESaT Malta; AELS NOCN; and Duolingo (accepted only with verification code). IMPORTANT RESTRICTION: "Note that MOI (Medium of Instruction) certificates are no longer accepted." — a Medium-of-Instruction letter from a previous school will NOT satisfy the requirement. The level is verified before enrolment by the University Language Centre (Centro Linguistico di Ateneo, www.cla.unina.it). Strong warning from the programme: "It is worth noting that if individual English proficiency testing is carried out after enrolment, the procedures at Embassies/Consulates for non-EU visas could fail" — i.e. non-EU applicants should hold the certificate BEFORE the visa stage rather than relying on a post-enrolment university test. An international English certificate is also explicitly noted as useful for visa issuance by the diplomatic representation.
application_deadline_eu: EU applicants (and non-EU applicants who already hold an Italian study visa) skip pre-admission entirely — "Selection for pre-admission: Not required / Not applicable" and "Application for visa: Not required / Not applicable". They go straight to final enrolment. Final enrolment window for a.y. 2026/27: 2026-07-15 to 2026-10-31, in person at the Student Office, Piazzale Tecchio 80, Naples — "Final enrollment starts on July 15th and ends on October 31th; however, it is likely (but not guaranteed) that the deadline for registration will be postponed to December." The orientation portal's generic university-wide text gives a slightly different opening date ("Enrollment and registration ... normally take place from July 26 to October 31 of each year"), so 2026-07-15 vs 2026-07-26 conflict — the programme-specific page (July 15) should prevail. Online enrolment is NOT allowed for EU non-Italian students (only Italian candidates may enrol online); everyone else must attend in person. Note the entry test (CEnT-S/TOLC) must be sat beforehand — CISIA sessions run in multiple sittings between February and October each year. Classes start 2026-09-14 (first term); second term starts in early March. As of the research date (2026-08-30) the 2026/27 EU enrolment window is OPEN. [uncertain]
application_deadline_non_eu: Non-EU applicants residing abroad who need a study visa must complete a pre-admission stage first. Programme page: "Selection for pre-admission: Expected start: January 2026. Expected closing date: 31 May 2026." The "Educational requirements" page instead describes it as "Pre-admission application (for non-EU students), open from February to June, articulated in selection groups", and the university-wide international admission regulation gives a later hard cut-off: "JUNE – 15 – 2026 – Pre-enrolment application deadline to University of Naples Federico II. After this date no programme changes are permitted. After this date pre-enrolment is allowed to the programmes with restricted access only." These three dates (31 May / "June" / 15 June 2026) conflict; the safe planning date is the earlier one, 2026-05-31. Visa application: submitted as soon as the pre-enrolment/pre-admission letter is issued; university-wide hard deadline "NOVEMBER – 30 – 2026 – Deadline for submitting the Visa Application at Italian Embassies/Consulates." Final enrolment (in person in Naples): 2026-07-15 to 2026-10-31, possibly extended to December. Classes start 2026-09-14. Concession for late visas: "in case of delayed visa issuing and consequent enrollment delay, the first semester of the first year can be attended online" — but examinations can only be taken in person after final enrolment, and attending online before final enrolment "does not accrue any right". As of the research date (2026-08-30) the 2026/27 non-EU pre-admission deadline has already passed; the next cycle (2027/28) is expected to open around January–February 2027. [uncertain]
required_documents: A) FOR NON-EU PRE-ADMISSION (submitted via the Universitaly portal; assessed by the Bachelor's Degree Coordinator): 1) Passport; 2) High School degree certificate (obtained after at least 12 years of pre-university education); 3) DOV (Declaration of Value) issued by the Italian embassy/consulate, OR a CIMEA comparability certificate; 4) English language certificate at CEFR B2 or higher; 5) the entry test result — the pre-admission page words this as "English TOLC-I with minimum score (10 out of 50)", while the pre-requisites page requires CEnT-S with minimum 9/45 (see entry_exam_or_test for this conflict). B) FOR IN-PERSON FINAL ENROLMENT in Naples: 1) Identity document/passport (shown + one copy left at the student office); 2) Proof of payment of tuition fees (e.g. bank counter deposit receipt) — in practice the regional tax plus the legal stamp; 3) Passport-size photograph in .jpeg format; 4) Visa permit (shown + one copy); 5) Permit of stay (permesso di soggiorno); 6) Copy of the pre-admission letter (shown + one copy); 7) Declaration of Value (DOV) or, alternatively, CIMEA certificate of comparability; 8) Copy of the high school diploma (shown + one copy); 9) Copy of the English language proficiency certificate; 10) Completed application form (the programme links a downloadable PDF form). C) FOR EU / VISA-EXEMPT APPLICANTS, the qualification assessment package sent to the Coordinator: translations, legalisations, Diploma Supplement, exam certificates, CIMEA certificate, and any Declaration of Value. D) FOR THE VISA APPOINTMENT at the Italian embassy: the Universitaly pre-enrolment summary validated by Federico II, language certificates, health insurance policy where applicable, and the foreign-qualification documents. Note: "The University of Naples Federico II does not issue admission letters for obtaining a visa" in the general university procedure — the EEIT programme itself issues a pre-admission/offer letter through the Universitaly workflow.
entry_exam_or_test: YES — a compulsory computer-based CISIA test. Primary specification (programme "Pre-Requisites" and "Educational requirements" pages): the CEnT-S, administered by the CISIA Interuniversity Consortium — the English-language scientific entry test. Structure for 2025-2026: 5 sections, 55 questions total — Mathematics 15 questions (30 min); Reasoning on texts and data 15 questions (30 min); Biology 10 questions (20 min); Chemistry 10 questions (20 min); Physics 5 questions (10 min). "However, to enroll to the Degree Programme, the answers to the Biology section are not considered!" Threshold: "For the purposes of enrolment, the candidate must reach the minimum threshold of 20% of the maximum score for the test (i.e. 9/45)" (Biology excluded from the score). OFA rule: "Admitted candidates who did not score more than 50% of the marks available for the Mathematics section of the test (i.e. 8/15) and at least 23/45 marks overall will be assigned an Additional Formative Obligation (OFA) that requires them to acquire at least 6 University Credits (CFU) in the MATH-03/A or MATH-02/B subject areas before being able to sit any other examinations. In any case, the educational debt must be cleared within the first year of the course." CONFLICTING OFFICIAL STATEMENTS: (i) the orientation portal fact-box says "Admission TOLC - I - OFA"; (ii) the pre-admission-letter page requires "English TOLC-I with minimum score (10 out of 50)"; (iii) the "How to enroll" page and the university news release describe a CISIA "Orientation and Self-Assessment Test" covering Mathematics, Sciences, Logic and Verbal Comprehension that is "compulsory but non-selective", with failure leading only to OFA. Test logistics: delivered online in multiple sessions between February and October each year at accredited computer laboratories of the School of Polytechnic and Basic Sciences; entry requirements are set jointly by the Engineering Board of that School for all its engineering degrees. Practice platform and session calendar via CISIA (cisiaonline.it) and scuolapsb.unina.it. No interview and no portfolio are required. [uncertain]
tuition_or_fees_link: https://eeit.dieti.unina.it/index.php/admission/tuition-fees — Fees are extremely low. Non-EU international students: "€140/year regional tax (compulsory) + €16,00 legal stamp (compulsory)" — the university describes tuition as "very affordable (almost null)". EU non-Italian students: "€200/year (university fees) + €140/year regional tax (compulsory) + €16,00 legal stamp (compulsory)". So the realistic annual cost is roughly €156 for non-EU and €356 for EU non-Italian students, before any ISEE-based variation for Italian residents. The page instructs applicants to confirm amounts with the Engineering student secretariat (Piazzale Tecchio 80). Scholarships: annual ADISURC (Campania regional right-to-study agency) calls for scholarships covering services and money — https://www.adisurcampania.it/borse-e-contributi/borse-di-studio — but "Access to scholarships requires having fully attained student status (final in presence enrollment has to be carried out)", so a scholarship cannot be secured before arriving and enrolling in person. The University of Naples "generally (not all years)" also offers its own scholarships to international students, published on the programme site when available. Scholarship page: https://eeit.dieti.unina.it/index.php/admission/scholarships

official_call_url: No dedicated bando/call (rectoral decree) exists for this programme, because it is an open-access (non-numerus-clausus) engineering degree — admission runs on the entry-test threshold plus the standard enrolment procedure rather than on a competitive ranking call. The governing official documents are: 1) the university's international admission regulation — https://www.international.unina.it/education/admission-regulation/ (carries the binding non-EU deadlines of 15 June 2026 for Universitaly pre-enrolment and 30 November 2026 for the visa application); 2) the official non-EU information notice "INFORMATION FOR NON-EU STUDENTS WITH RESIDENCY ABROAD WHO WISH TO ENROL IN A DEGREE PROGRAMME AT THE UNIVERSITY OF NAPLES FEDERICO II" — https://www.unina.it/documents/20117/4260320/UniversItaly_2026_27.pdf ; 3) the Enrolment and Tuition Fee Payment Guide (Guide dello Studente) — https://www.unina.it/didattica/sportello-studenti/guide-dello-studente ; 4) engineering entry-test admission notices from the School — http://www.scuolapsb.unina.it/index.php/studiare-al-napoli/ammissione-ai-corsi (Italian only). The non-EU application itself is filed on the national Universitaly portal: https://www.universitaly.it/studenti-stranieri
seats_total: Not published. No numerus clausus or seat number appears on any official Federico II page for this programme. The programme states only that "The Programme Teaching Committee normally defines the admission criteria and any enrolment limits, without prejudice to any different provisions established by law", i.e. a cap could in principle be set but none has been announced for a.y. 2026/27. Unlike Medicine and Surgery (ENG) or Biology for One Health, this degree is not listed as a "numero programmato" course. Prospective applicants should treat it as open-access subject to the entry-test threshold, and confirm with the Degree Programme Director (Prof. Fabio Villone, fabio.villone@unina.it) or uff.didattica.dieti@unina.it. [uncertain]
non_eu_reserved_seats: Not published. Federico II's international admission regulation and the UniversItaly 2026/27 notice do not give a per-programme non-EU reserved quota (contingente riservato) for this degree, and the programme's own admission pages give none. Non-EU applicants are instead filtered by the pre-admission assessment (documents + English B2 + entry-test score) rather than by a fixed numerical quota. Confirmation should be sought from uff.didattica.dieti@unina.it or the Universitaly programme record for the relevant intake year. [uncertain]

uncertainty_notes:
1) ACCREDITATION STATUS — CONTRADICTION BETWEEN TWO OFFICIAL UNINA SOURCES, and it resolves in the applicant's favour. The orientation portal (orientamento.unina.it) still prints the tag '(in fase di accreditamento)' inside the programme title as of 2026-08-30, which literally means the course is still going through accreditation and opening is not guaranteed. However, the programme's own site (eeit.dieti.unina.it, a unina.it subdomain) states the course 'has been approved by both the Italian National University Council (CUN) and by the National University Evaluation Agency (ANVUR)' and announces 'Lessons will start on Sept 14th 2026'. A published start date plus CUN+ANVUR approval indicates accreditation is effectively complete and the orientation-portal label is stale. Treat the programme as launching for a.y. 2026/27, but the stale tag should be re-checked before advising a client.

2) ENTRY TEST — THREE DIFFERENT OFFICIAL DESCRIPTIONS. (a) 'Pre-Requisites' and 'Educational requirements' pages: CEnT-S (CISIA English-language scientific test), 55 questions in 5 sections, Biology excluded from scoring, minimum 9/45, called 'the compulsory selective test'. (b) 'Asking for the pre-admission letter' page: 'English TOLC-I with minimum score (10 out of 50)'. (c) 'How to enroll' page and the unina.it news release: a CISIA 'Orientation and Self-Assessment Test' that is 'compulsory but non-selective', with OFA as the only consequence of a poor result. The orientation-portal fact-box adds a fourth label, 'TOLC - I - OFA'. CEnT-S and English TOLC-I are related but distinct CISIA products with different maximum scores (45 scored vs 50). Applicants must confirm with DIETI which test to book before paying a CISIA registration fee — booking the wrong one is a real risk. Flagged as uncertain.

3) SELECTIVE vs NON-SELECTIVE — flows from (2). If the CEnT-S threshold (9/45) is genuinely enforced for enrolment, the test is a pass/fail gate even though there is no competitive ranking. The 'non-selective' wording likely refers to the absence of a ranking-based numerus clausus, not to the absence of a minimum score. Practical guidance: assume a minimum score IS required.

4) NON-EU DEADLINE — THREE DATES. Programme page: pre-admission closes 31 May 2026. Educational-requirements page: pre-admission 'open from February to June'. University-wide international regulation: Universitaly pre-enrolment deadline 15 June 2026. The programme-level date (31 May) is the earlier and safer planning date; the 15 June date is the university-wide administrative cut-off. Also note the programme calls its January-2026 start and 31 May close 'Expected', so these were provisional at publication.

5) EU ENROLMENT OPENING DATE — 15 July (programme page) vs 26 July (generic university text reproduced on the orientation portal). Minor, but the programme-specific date should prevail.

6) SEATS — no seats_total and no non_eu_reserved_seats are published anywhere on unina.it for this programme. This is consistent with an open-access engineering degree, but it means neither figure could be verified. The programme reserves the right to set enrolment limits via its Teaching Committee.

7) TIMING OF THIS RESEARCH — data captured 2026-08-30. The 2026/27 non-EU pre-admission window (closing 31 May / 15 June 2026) has already passed; the EU in-person enrolment window (15 July – 31 Oct 2026) is currently open. All dates above are for the FIRST intake (a.y. 2026/27); the 2027/28 cycle is expected to open around January–February 2027 and dates will need re-verification.

8) DIPLOMA NAME — this is a standalone English-medium degree, not an English curriculum inside an Italian-titled degree, so there is no divergent Italian diploma name to report. No Italian denominazione was published on the official pages consulted.

9) CONTACT EMAIL GAP — the programme's own 'Admission schedule' page shows an unrendered placeholder ('EMAILDAAGGINSEGUITO') instead of a contact address, so the working contacts are the Degree Programme Director (fabio.villone@unina.it), uff.didattica.dieti@unina.it, and the Engineering student secretariat (segreing@unina.it).

10) MOI CERTIFICATES REJECTED — worth flagging to any applicant from a country where English-medium instruction letters are the norm; only the listed certificate bodies (including Duolingo with verification code) are accepted.
